# Rakazo [English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](./README.ja.md) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/elie222/rakazo?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&color=2563EB)](https://github.com/elie222/rakazo/stargazers) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20the%20community-5865F2?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/RWwKa2Sn7h) [![Download on the App Store](https://img.shields.io/badge/App%20Store-Download%20for%20iPhone-black?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099) [![Get Android on Google Play](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Play-Get%20the%20app-black?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=googleplay&logoColor=white)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app) ![Rakazo — AI teammates you actually own](./docs/readme-hero.png) Rakazo is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot. Persistent AI teammates with their own memory, routines, apps, and computer. Run it on your own machine, with your own model. Use it on the [web](https://app.rakazo.com), [desktop](https://rakazo.com/download/), [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099), and [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app). It is also an alternative to Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and Claude Duet. Learn more at [rakazo.com](https://rakazo.com). ## Features - Routines - Memory - Computer and browser use - Private or shared team computers - Sandboxes in Docker, the cloud, or on your own machine - Group chats - Delegation and subagents - Builds dashboards and docs you can share by link - Voice chat and calls - Any model, with your own keys - Thousands of app integrations, plus MCP
### Every bot gets a computer A browser, terminal, files, and a full desktop. Watch it work, take control to sign in, and hand it back. ### Bots that work together Put bots in a group and @mention them. They split the work, check each other, and report back.
### Routines Run a bot on a schedule, from an email, or from a webhook, and see every run. ### Pages Bots build live dashboards and documents you can open full screen, share, and ask about.
### Connected apps Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear and thousands more, plus your own MCP servers and OpenAPI tools. ### On every device Web, desktop, iPhone, and Android, all talking to the same server.
## Quick start (published images) You need Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL. No clone or Node install. ```bash mkdir -p rakazo && cd rakazo && curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elie222/rakazo/main/infra/compose/install-images.sh && bash install-images.sh ``` The installer downloads the Compose files, creates `.env` with random secrets, and starts Rakazo. It preserves an existing `.env` when rerun. Open [http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173), create an account, and connect a model. Local Docker computers are on by default. Optional remote providers: `e2b`, `novita`, `daytona`, `createos`, `boat`, `boxd`, or `railway` with the matching API key. Default image tag is `edge` (main builds, `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`). Details and tags: [self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md#published-images-no-checkout). On restricted networks, override the installer download base (`RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_BASE`), skip existing Compose files (`--local` / `RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_EXISTING`), or mirror the bootstrap script URL — see [Restricted networks / mirror downloads](./docs/self-host.md#restricted-networks--mirror-downloads). For an agent-assisted install, use [SETUP_PROMPT.md](./SETUP_PROMPT.md). ## Run on a server Bots stay on when the backend runs on a server. Use the same installer on a VPS, then connect from the desktop app, the mobile app, or a browser. ```bash bash install-images.sh --prepare-only # edit .env: SANDBOX_PROVIDER=boat (or e2b / daytona / createos) with its API key, RAKAZO_HOST=your.domain bash install-images.sh ``` Put HTTPS in front of port 5173; [docs/self-host-production.md](./docs/self-host-production.md#public-single-vm-deployment) covers the Caddy setup and host hardening. In the desktop app choose **Existing instance** and enter the `https://` address. Or [deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/new/template/rakazo-template); see the [Railway setup guide](./infra/railway/README.md). ## Local development (source checkout) You need Node.js 24.15.0 or newer in the 24.x line, or Node.js 26+; pnpm 12; and Docker. Node.js 25.x is not supported. ```bash git clone https://github.com/elie222/rakazo.git cd rakazo cp .env.example .env ``` Set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD` to two values from `openssl rand -hex 16`, then put them in `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`. The app connects as its own `rakazo_app` login, which row-level security applies to; migrations run as the owner ([database roles](docs/self-host-configuration.md#database-roles)). Set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET` to independent long random values. Docker sandboxes also need a dedicated `SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN`. You can also set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or connect a supported model provider during onboarding. For host-side development with Docker Desktop, set `SANDBOX_CONTROL_VIA_LOOPBACK=true` in `.env`. The supervisor discovers Docker Desktop's user socket automatically; `DOCKER_HOST` or `DOCKER_SOCKET` can override it for another Docker runtime. Managed app catalogs are optional. Set `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` for Composio, or the `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_ID`, `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `PIPEDREAM_PROJECT_ID` trio for Pipedream Connect. Users can add an HTTPS MCP server or OpenAPI JSON document from **Integrations** without enabling either managed catalog. Connector credentials are encrypted on the server and are never returned by the API. Paid data services (map places, search results, work emails, profiles, SEO data) are optional too. Set `PAID_SERVICES_PROVIDER=treg` and `PAID_SERVICES_API_KEY` to an org-scoped [Treg](https://treg.to) token, and bots can find and call them on the deployment's account. When model credits are on, each call is charged to the organization's credits at the provider's cost plus 20%. ```bash pnpm install pnpm sandbox:build pnpm dev ``` `pnpm dev` uses the Postgres in `DATABASE_URL` when it accepts a connection. Otherwise it starts a local `rakazo-dev-postgres` container with Docker, and every checkout reuses that one. It applies migrations and generates the Prisma client before starting. A branch that adds migrations main doesn't have gets its own database on the same server, copied from the shared one when possible, so unmerged schema changes stay out of it. When the default ports are taken, for example by another git worktree, it moves to the next free block and prints the URL. Set `WEB_PORT` and `API_PORT` to choose ports yourself. To try a checkout from your phone or another computer, install [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) on each device and set `RAKAZO_DEV_TAILNET=1` in `.env`. `pnpm dev` then serves the web app over HTTPS at `https://..ts.net:`, reachable only from devices on your tailnet, and stops serving it when you quit. Sign in at that URL on every device, including the one running it. The first run may ask you to turn on HTTPS certificates for your tailnet. To keep keys in a secrets manager instead of `.env`, set `RAKAZO_DEV_RUN_WITH` to the command that runs another with your secrets added, for example `op run --env-file=dev.env --` or `infisical run --env=dev --projectId= --`. `pnpm dev` then starts inside it, and the values it adds win over `.env`. To run Postgres from the Compose file instead, start it with the `postgres-host` overlay, which publishes loopback `127.0.0.1:5433`, and point `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` at it: ```bash docker compose --env-file .env \ -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml \ -f infra/compose/docker-compose.postgres-host.yml \ up postgres -d ``` Use a URI-safe `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (`openssl rand -hex 16`). An existing `pgdata` volume keeps the user, password, and database from first init, so keep those values in `.env`, or change them in place with `ALTER ROLE` / rename. Recreate the volume only after a backup (or when the data is disposable); `docker compose down -v` deletes all Postgres state. Open the printed URL ([http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173) by default), create an account, connect a model, and create your first bot. For deployment, provider selection, backups, and upgrades, see the [self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md), [production deployment](./docs/self-host-production.md), [backup and restore](./docs/self-host-backups.md), and [upgrading](./docs/self-host-upgrading.md). To use CreateOS, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=createos` and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_API_KEY`. Optional `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_BASE_URL`, `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_SHAPE`, and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_ROOTFS` default to `https://api.sb.createos.sh`, `s-2vcpu-2gb`, and `desktop:1`. To use Railway computers, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=railway`, `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN` and `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID` on the API and worker. Choose the sandbox environment explicitly; Railway's automatic environment ID identifies the hosted app's environment. Use the narrowest Railway API token that works: prefer a project token if sufficient for sandbox operations and supported by the client's authentication. This provider currently uses bearer authentication, so use a team/workspace token rather than a personal account token. The live screen and desktop require `PRIVATE` networking so Railway's public domain can serve the screen. Computers use this mode and can reach other services in the same Railway project/environment, as well as the public internet. We recommend a dedicated Railway project (or at least a separate environment) for sandboxes, separate from the app and database. Recreate existing `ISOLATED` computers before use. The desktop is installed on first start. Stopping a computer saves its portable home and destroys the sandbox; the next start restores that home in a new sandbox. Railway sandbox usage is metered. New computers start in Railway's default region. Set `RAILWAY_SANDBOX_REGION` (for example `asia-southeast1-eqsg3a`) to keep them near the API; a running computer moves on its next start. Workspace exports reject files above 64 MiB without truncating them. Set `RAILWAY_MAX_WORKSPACE_FILE_BYTES` to change this limit. ## Desktop and mobile The Electron and Expo apps are clients of the same Rakazo API used by the web app. With the development stack running, launch Electron with: ```bash pnpm --filter @rakazo/desktop dev ``` On first run the desktop app asks whether to run Rakazo on this computer or connect to an existing server. **This computer** installs and starts the published images with Docker Compose (the same files as `infra/compose/install-images.sh`) under the app's data directory, so Docker Desktop, OrbStack, or Docker Engine must be installed; the app links to them when it is not. Installed builds pin the image tag to their own version; unpackaged builds pull `edge`. Developers running `pnpm dev` should pick **Existing instance** with `http://127.0.0.1:5173` instead. Public servers must use HTTPS; HTTP is accepted only for loopback and private LAN addresses (not link-local). The app verifies Rakazo's health endpoint before saving, and later launches go straight to that instance. The stack keeps running after the app quits; **Stop Local Stack** in the application menu turns it off. On Linux the desktop app ships as an AppImage, which needs FUSE 2 (`libfuse.so.2`). Distributions that only include FUSE 3, such as Fedora Silverblue or Ubuntu 24.04, show `dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`. Install the FUSE 2 library (`fuse-libs` on Fedora, `libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04, `libfuse2` on older Ubuntu and Debian), or run the AppImage without FUSE: ```bash chmod +x Rakazo-*.AppImage ./Rakazo-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run ``` **This computer** looks for the `docker` CLI and does not detect Podman. To try another Docker-compatible CLI that supports the `compose` commands, set `RAKAZO_DOCKER_BINARY` to its path before starting the app. Use **Change Rakazo Server…** in the application menu to reconnect. Closing that window without saving returns to the previous instance. For development automation, set `RAKAZO_WEB_URL` to point the shell somewhere else without changing the saved instance, or `RAKAZO_FORCE_SETUP=1` to run setup again. Mobile build and release instructions live in [docs/mobile-release.md](./docs/mobile-release.md). ## UI language The web (and Electron-hosted) UI supports English, Deutsch, 한국어, Türkçe, हिन्दी, Português (Brasil), 简体中文, 繁體中文, Español, Русский, Français, עברית, Nederlands, 日本語, and Polski under **Settings → Language**. The Expo app ships English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, Русский, Deutsch, Nederlands, 日本語, Español, and Polski catalogs, and **Account → Language** lists all nine. A device language or `EXPO_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_UI_LOCALE` still selects the starting catalog before a saved choice. Native Electron setup and menus also support the web UI's languages, following the saved app choice or, on first launch, the system language. The marketing homepage (`apps/www`) offers all 15 languages through footer links, including `/zh/` and `/zh-tw/`; other marketing pages remain primarily English. ## Development ```text apps/ web, api, worker, desktop, mobile, and public website packages/ domain, contracts, persistence, adapters, UI, and test tooling infra/ local services and computer images docs/ architecture, operations, and release guides ``` Common checks: ```bash pnpm lint pnpm check pnpm test pnpm test:integration pnpm test:e2e ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow and test matrix. ## Documentation Chinese guides cover [self-hosting](./docs/zh-CN/self-host.md), [models](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-models.md), [backups](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-backups.md), [upgrading](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-upgrading.md), and [restricted networks](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-restricted-network.md). - TypeScript - React 19, Vite, and Tailwind CSS - Electron and Expo - Hono and oRPC - PostgreSQL and Prisma - Better Auth - Graphile Worker - Pi - Docker, E2B, Daytona, CreateOS, and Boat - Composio, Pipedream Connect, MCP, and OpenAPI integrations ## Contributing Contributions are welcome.
